attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: In context, 'it' means that scaling did not and will not get to AGI. The normalised version keeps 'starting to' and the field-level scope.

contract.note: The plain reading (a visible, growing trend in 2025, not consensus) is an ordinary reading of 'starting to realize'. It is not stretched for or against the speaker.

evidence.note: March 2025 AAAI survey: 76% of respondents thought scaling current systems unlikely to reach AGI. This shows substantial acceptance, though not growth over time.
Nov 2025: Sutskever, a leading scaling figure, publicly rejected the idea that 100x more scale would transform things. A prominent statement inside the period.
NeurIPS's own programme notice: Sutton's keynote argued the field had lost its way and needs new approaches. Indirect support: it is not explicitly about scaling and AGI.
Vinyals (DeepMind) pushed back on limits to pre-training scaling, so the view was not universal. But he calls 'scaling is over' a popular belief, which fits a growing trend.

reviews.rationale: Within 2025, a large AAAI survey majority doubted that scaling would reach AGI. Sutskever publicly declared a return to research, and Sutton's NeurIPS keynote called for new approaches. Frontier-lab pushback (e4) shows there was no consensus, but the claim only says 'starting to', and e4 itself calls the view popular. The support condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The normalised version matches the sentence. In context, though, 'it' is the scale-is-all-you-need view, which Marcus defines in the same post as reaching general intelligence by scaling alone.

contract.note: The contract tests a weaker view: that scaling was the main strategy for progress. It explicitly drops the AGI-by-scaling content Marcus gave the view. That stretches the claim in the speaker's favour, and the result turns on this substitution.

evidence.note: Sutskever calls 2020–2025 the 'age of scaling'. This supports scaling as the dominant research strategy over the half decade, not belief that it would reach AGI.
Sutskever says companies favoured scaling as a low-risk way to invest resources. This supports the investment strand, though it is an interview account, not a measurement.
Epoch AI (May 2024): compute grew 4-5x a year, and about two-thirds of language model gains came from scale. This supports scaling as the central research strategy.
The 2025 US AI Action Plan calls advanced compute essential. This loosely supports a policy focus on compute, not on the AGI-by-scaling thesis itself.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows that scaling was the main practical strategy in 2020–2025 and shaped research, investment and US compute policy. But the claim concerns the scale-is-all-you-need view as Marcus defined it: scaling alone reaches general intelligence. The packet has no evidence that this stronger view was dominant, and the contract's weaker reading is not a fair substitute. The claim is therefore not settled.
